Outline.md
# Outline — what the paper says and what carries it (revision 1)

Source: `idea-repo` Brief revision 4 (the idea, the predictions P1–P5, the study design and cell budget), the objective (`story-repo`#1) and `prior_work.md`. This page says *what to test and where it shows*, never what a result must be. Every claim below has a "refuted if" line; a result that triggers it changes the claim, and I take it to `idea-repo` (see "When results do not carry it").

## 1. The story in one paragraph
Regression-adjustment estimators of the global average treatment effect (GATE) under network interference (Chin 2019; Han–Ugander 2023) fit outcome on functions of the assignment (own treatment, treated-neighbour fraction, …) and predict at all-treated and all-control. Published work shows they *can* work but gives no account of *how well, why, and when not*. We treat the estimator as **extrapolation from the observed exposure distribution to the two global corners** and ask what that predicts. The error splits into a **variance part** (OLS leverage of the corner contrast, scaling like d/(p(1−p)n)) and a **bias part** (curvature of the response × raw distance of the corner from the observed exposure support, roughly *not* growing with degree). The two parts have different drivers and can move in opposite directions with degree, so "error grows with degree" is true only where noise dominates. We test these scalings across interference mechanisms, graph families (synthetic and two real Facebook graphs), treatment probabilities and designs (Bernoulli, graph-cluster); map where regression beats and loses to difference-in-means (DM) and to exposure-mapping HT/Hájek; ask whether flexible/data-adaptive learners help; and test a data-computable two-part diagnostic against pre-registered trivial predictors. Not a new estimator: a verified, predictive account of when to trust an existing one. Positive, negative and mixed outcomes are all reported.

## 2. Position against prior work (Related work, one paragraph per cluster)
- *Regression GATE estimators*: Chin 2019 (estimator; Fig. 2 already shows the exposure-distribution mismatch qualitatively and draws the off-policy analogy), Han–Ugander 2023 (covariate generation/selection, block bootstrap). **We do not claim the extrapolation viewpoint as new**; we claim the quantified decomposition, its tests across mechanisms/graphs/designs, the regime map including where regression loses, and the diagnostic. Wording "to our knowledge within the literature checked".
- *Design-based exposure-mapping estimators*: Aronow–Samii 2017, Eckles et al. 2017, Ugander et al. 2013 (baselines and designs); Gao–Ding 2023 (regression for exposure-mapping estimands under overlap — different estimand; read in detail before the text states the difference); Thiyageswaran et al. 2024 and Shirani–Bayati 2024 (data-adaptive exposure / message-passing competitors).
- *Misspecification / unknown interference*: Sävje et al. 2021, Leung 2022, Sävje 2023, Yu et al. 2022 — our setting is estimand = GATE with a possibly wrong response model.
- *Designs*: Karrer et al. 2021, Cortez et al. 2022 (optional), Chen et al. 2023, Leung 2022 rate. *Overlap/positivity*: Crump 2009, D'Amour 2021 (where the extrapolation analogy comes from).
`report` reads each source before attributing a theorem (`prior_work.md` says several were read by abstract only).

## 3. Claims, the evidence each needs, the figure that carries it
Cells refer to the Brief's cell budget (core = SBM n≈3000, 6 mechanisms (a)–(f), s=0.5, d∈{5,20,80}, p∈{0.25,0.5,0.75}, σ=0.5; slices around it). Main-text figures use only cells that exist in the analysis plan; `analysis` confirms or cuts the cell list and tells me which claims lose support.

**C0 (setup, not a finding) — the harness is valid.** Exact GATE at the corners; every mechanism calibrated to τ=1 and spillover share s; with σ=0 and correct spec the error is 0; DM bias equals sτ under Bernoulli. *Evidence*: 
[truncated for publication]

cd /hutian/tmp && cat > plan1.md <<'EOF'
# Review of the Outline (revision 1) and the plan it implies — round 1

Reviewer: `idea-review-repo`. Read: the Outline as of 2026-11-25 19:18, Brief revision 4 (cell budget and P5 rule), the objective and `deliverable.md`. The Outline is a good frame: one claim per figure, a "refuted if" line for every claim, negative results in-line, "not new" wording stated up front, tiers kept apart. Nothing below asks for less; most items are *cells or claims that the evidence you list needs and the cell budget does not contain*. Each item names the claim it touches.

## A. Figures promised that the cell budget cannot produce (fix with `analysis`; first three change what is run)

1. **C4 / Figure 1 (headline): a heat map of log(RMSE_reg/RMSE_DM) over (s, mechanism) with a sign-flip contour.** The cell list has s ∈ {0.25, 0.75} only on mechanisms (a) and (c); the other four mechanisms exist only at s=0.5 (plus the s=0 null). The map over six mechanisms × s does not exist, and a contour from 3–4 s-values is coarse. The break-even s* also depends on σ, n, d, p, but σ varies only on (a),(c). Cheap fix, since Tier G fits cost ms: a fine s grid (e.g. 0, 0.1, …, 0.9) × 6 mechanisms at the core d and p=½ (~60 cells), and σ ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1} on that row for the two or three mechanisms that matter. State s* as a function of σ, d, p as the result, not only a map.
2. **C1 / Figure 2: log-log fits of RMSE on n.** No cell varies n (the core is SBM n≈3000). Both the Brief (P1, "log n") and C1 depend on it. Add an n slice (e.g. 1000, 3000, 10000) on (a) and (c), core d, p; with only d ∈ {5, 20, 80} the d-exponent has three points, so also report it with a CI and say so.
3. **C5 / Figure 6: "a band that is a function of cluster resolution and realised cluster quality, not the graph's name", and the Brief's P3 "loses the benefit on low-modularity graphs".** Cluster designs are run only on the SBM core (3 mechanisms × 3 resolutions × 3 d = 27). A band in *quality* needs graphs of different modularity under the cluster design: add cluster cells on ER (no structure), SBM at a weaker mixing parameter, ego-Facebook and Stanford3 (detected communities), for two mechanisms and two resolutions. Without them C5 can only say "on this SBM".
4. **C7: "degree varied by edge thinning / k-core" on real graphs.** The 12 real-graph cells are two graphs × six mechanisms at one setting; no thinning cells exist. Add a thinning slice (Stanford3 at 3 retained-edge fractions × (a),(c)) with the covariates the Brief says to report, or drop the sentence.
5. **C3 mirror response.** C3 predicts the bias minimiser shifts for "saturating and mirror" responses. Only the concave saturating response (c) exists (d is a threshold). Either add a convex mirror of (c) as a labelled exploratory mechanism (one extra mechanism on the p grid, 5 cells), or state that only the saturating direction is tested.
6. **Coverage and inference have no claim.** The Brief's metrics and P5 ("flags failure better than the bootstrap CI, whose coverage collapses exactly where L is large") and the objective's "report uncertainty" both lead to the question A/B practitioners care about: does the nominal 95% CI cover? There is no claim, figure or table for coverage/width of the unit and cluster bootstrap, of the graph-aware variance, and of the oracle. Add a claim (coverage vs L and vs bias/SD across cells; the bootstrap SE is already a P5 benchmark) and say which figure or table carries it. Sign-error rate is in the metrics but in no figure either; a column in Table 3 or the regime map's second panel is enough.

## B. The diagnostic claim C6 as stated cannot be decided by the core grid (also sent to `idea-repo`)
On the core grid (equal-degree SBM, Bernoulli) L ≈ (1+d)/(p(1−p)) is a function of (d, p), and the Brief's benchmark "n·p(1−p)/d" is, up to the +1 and n, its reciprocal. Part (i) therefore cannot beat that benchmark on those cells (their R² are essentially identical),

shown.message:
I reviewed the Outline (revision 1) and sent the review to `story-repo` as #3. One item also went to `idea-repo` as #5, because it changes the Brief's P5 rule.

The Outline is a good frame. Each claim has one figure and a "refuted if" line, negative results are reported in-line, and what is not new is stated up front. The problems are mostly figures and claims that the Brief's cell budget can't produce:

- **Missing cells.**
  - The headline regime map (Figure 1) needs the spillover share s varied on all six mechanisms. The budget varies it only on two.
  - The log-log fits on n need an n sweep, and none exists.
  - The cluster-design claim needs cluster cells on graphs of different modularity. Only the stochastic block model (SBM) core has them.
  - There are no edge-thinning cells on the real graphs.
  - The "mirror response" in the treatment-probability claim has no mechanism to test it.
- **No coverage claim.** The Outline has no claim, figure or table for confidence-interval coverage. The objective's request to report uncertainty and the Brief's P5 both lead to it.
- **P5 part (i), also sent to `idea-repo`.** On the equal-degree core grid the leverage L is a function of (d, p) alone, and one pre-registered benchmark is essentially its reciprocal. Part (i) cannot beat that benchmark there, so P5 would come out "not supported" for a reason unrelated to the diagnostic. It should be judged on the cells where L and the benchmarks differ, such as BA, cluster designs and the real graphs.
- **Evidence at the planned size.**
  - At d=80, 200 draws give a weak test of the claim that bias is independent of d. I suggested at least 1000 draws, since fits cost milliseconds.
  - The numbers of graph, assignment and noise draws need stating.
  - Tier A (100 draws) and Tier G (200 draws) need the same draws in any figure that compares them.
  - The analysis plan should be committed before the first non-pilot run.
- **Scope wording.** The real graphs should appear in the regime map, not only in the robustness section. Cortez and Yu should not be listed as compared unless they are run.

I'll review again when the Outline changes or the analysis plan appears. Commitment #2 stays open for that.
